newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast products fall with NYMEX, thin trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast products fall with NYMEX, thin trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices fell about two cents across the board as collapsing futures markets spooked traders and kept them sidelined late.
Persian Gulf sources denied bearish reports that the U.S. asked Saudi Arabia to compensate for lost Iraqi exports by increasing crude oil production.
Overall easing of Mideast tensions helped push NYMEX October crude down $1.32 a barrel to $23.19.
"It paralyzed the market," one broker said, forecasting little trade until Wednesday, after the market absorbs nationwide inventory data.
Conventional or "clear" grade gasoline in Los Angeles fell about two cents from midday to range 68.00/69.00 cents a gallon.

And Premium conventional in L.A. rose one cent to hold a 10 cent advantage over regular. Tightened supplies resulted from the early September shutdown of Mobil's Torrance refinery reformer, which upgrades gasolines.
Ultra-clean CARB gasoline also eased about two cents 71/72 cents after rising slightly Friday.
Low sulphur diesel in L.A. edged down two cents for bids and one cent for offers, leaving assessments at 71/73 cents a gallon.
San Francisco distillates and gasolines were assessed two cents lower than L.A. material.
And pricey distillates in the Pacific Northwest were poised to fall this week as cargoes headed toward the region.
